text: Rollback strategies — two genuinely different things hiding behind one word.
A code rollback is simple — revert and redeploy through machinery already built. A data rollback is harder — the bad code already wrote real rows and showed real numbers before anyone noticed.
Rolling back code and even data still can't un-send an alert that already reached someone, or un-make a decision a dispatcher already acted on. That's exactly why mitigation matters as its own step.
Rollback is fast when the previous version was genuinely fine. A forward fix is sometimes faster when the bug is small and well understood. Choose whichever actually gets to correct sooner.
Rollback isn't automatically the safe default. Next up: documentation that actually gets used — preventing the next incident from being a mystery.
